Users viewing the topic live are not told their notification level changed (no /topic/<id> MessageBus publish), and the 'muted if already regular' toggle behavior lives in a second place future changes must update; whoever changes TopicUser.change's semantics next gets silently divergent behavior from this path.

This introduces duplicated notification-level toggle semantics in a second place and bypasses the existing MessageBus publish side-effect, so other live clients/subscriptions won’t receive a `notification_level_change` event from this path.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` triple-stash renders unescaped HTML built from the user-controlled topic title (`model.fancyTitle` interpolated into the I18n string containing `{{title}}`), so any markup present in fancyTitle is injected straight into the page. The safe pattern is to keep `` in the translation and use a normal `{{title}}` interpolation rather than making the whole string HTML.

records.stripped_text: [ADVISORY] `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` triple-stash renders unescaped HTML built from the user-controlled topic title (`model.fancyTitle` interpolated into the I18n string containing `{{title}}`), so any markup present in fancyTitle is injected straight into the page. A user who can create or rename topics controls the title that lands in this unescaped sink; if fancy_title does not fully strip or escape angle-bracket markup (it preserves some HTML/entities by design), the unsubscribe page for that topic becomes an XSS vector for anyone who receives the notification email and clicks through. The safe pattern is to keep `` in the translation and use a normal `{{title}}` interpolation rather than making the whole string HTML.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe action calls tu.notification_level on a nil TopicUser record, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 where the unsubscribe link promises a working page. Any user who received a notification email but has no TopicUser row for that topic (e.g., never visited the topic, row never created) clicks the emailed unsubscribe link and gets a raw 500 instead of the unsubscribe confirmation page; the level is never changed and no error state is shown.
records.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the code dereferences `current_user.id` without any guard: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])`. If `current_user` is nil (anonymous/logged-out), this will raise `NoMethodError`. The diff also adds the action to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` (`only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`) and the routes are plain GETs (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`), but no login requirement is shown in this diff, so the failure mode described is directly supported by the added code.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe route performs current_user.id without any authentication guard, so an anonymous visitor following the emailed link crashes the controller. A user who clicks the unsubscribe link from an email client without an active Discourse session (the common case — email links are opened logged-out) hits TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], nil) then current_user.id on nil, producing a 500 instead of a login redirect or 4xx.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The unsubscribe state mutation is performed via an unauthenticated-by-design GET request and bypasses TopicUser.change, so no MessageBus notification_level_change message is published. Users who complete unsubscribe on one device keep seeing the stale notification level on an already-open topic tab (no /topic/:id message pushes the change), and crawlers/prefetchers (e.g., email scanners prefetching GET links) can flip a user's notification level silently if a session cookie rides along; the mutation should go through TopicUser.change or be POST with a token.
records.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff directly mutates and saves `TopicUser` (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`) instead of calling `TopicUser.change(...)` (which elsewhere in the diff publishes `MessageBus` on `/topic/#{topic_id}` when `attrs[:notification_level]` is set). This introduces duplicated notification-level toggle semantics in a second place and bypasses the existing MessageBus publish side-effect, so other live clients/subscriptions won’t receive a `notification_level_change` event from this path.
